changelog: Fix: 2026_09_17_0003's tolerance audit (added v3.12.1) false-positived on live, flagging trades 87/88 (BTCUSDT Long, entries at 2026-08-20 11:42:45 and 11:47:10, 4.5 minutes apart) as a possible duplicate. Both are genuine, independent positions present in Bitfunded's own Position History -- not a duplicate. Time proximity on (pair, direction) alone cannot distinguish a duplicate (one execution recorded twice) from a legitimate fast re-entry (two different executions close together) -- ordinary trading behavior, not an anomaly

Fix: the audit now also requires entry_price and pnl to match exactly before treating two rows as the same execution -- what an actual duplicate shares that a re-entry doesn't. Trades 87/88 have different entry_price (71962.10 vs 71968.30) and different pnl (+0.74 vs -0.43); the corrected audit does not flag them. 0003's state-detection design from v3.12.3 (one ZEC row already correct -> no-op; two -> repair) is unchanged -- only the trailing audit's matching rule was wrong

Edited 2026_09_17_0003 directly rather than routing around it -- it was still status='failed' on live (this exact false positive is what failed it), so per the rule v3.12.2 established, this is the retry path the runner is built for, not a checksum-lock violation

CLAUDE.md: corrected the v3.12.1 migration checklist entry, which documented the wrong heuristic (time proximity alone). A duplicate-detection check now needs (pair, direction) + a time window + entry_price + pnl all matching
